history.idea: Replace the random baseline with a filter-then-fill curator. (1) Build a word-level TF-IDF (or hashed unigram+bigram) logistic-regression classifier: positives = the 200 target_sample docs (plus their halves/chunks to get more examples), negatives = a seeded random sample of ~3000 pool docs; score every pool doc. Combine with cheap structural features of the target domain (WikiText style): doc starts with '= Title =' on line 1, presence of ' @-@ ', ' , ' and ' . ' spaced punctuation. (2) Remove damaged docs: detect word-shuffled articles (the pool contains wiki-looking docs whose words are scrambled within sentences) by scoring each doc with a bigram model fit on target_sample plus clearly-clean high-scoring docs — e.g. fraction of adjacent word bigrams in the doc that appear in the target-sample bigram set, or mean per-token bigram log-prob with add-k smoothing; shuffled docs have far lower bigram hit rate than clean ones at the same unigram similarity, so threshold at the valley of the bimodal distribution among wiki-style docs (fallback: drop the bottom mode via 2-means on the hit rate). Also drop spam templates ('discount code', 'coupon', 'free shipping'), docs with high non-ASCII/homoglyph ratio, and very short docs. (3) Deduplicate exactly and near-exactly (hash of normalized first 200 chars + hash of whole text; keep one copy). (4) Keep all surviving clean wiki-style docs, ranked by classifier score; count tokens with tiktoken gpt2 (or estimate len/4 if time is tight). If the kept set has fewer than T tokens, do NOT pad with junk — return just the kept set in a seeded shuffled order so the trainer cycles it; only if the kept set is under ~0.35 T, top up with the next-best-scoring non-spam, non-shuffled docs. If more than T, take the top-scoring T tokens' worth. Shuffle the final order with CURATE_SEED.
history.outcome: dev 1.8300 against 1.9607 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Extend damage detection from the document head to the whole document. Today the non-ASCII/homoglyph, alpha-ratio, repetition and spam checks only read the first 3000 chars, and the shuffle check reads only two 300-word segments (start and middle). Change: for every doc that currently passes `wiki & ~bad`, split the full word list into consecutive 300-word segments (cap at 40 evenly spaced segments for time; merge a trailing segment under 100 words into the previous one). Per segment compute (a) bigram hit rate against the final bigram set (B2 if pass 2 ran, else B), (b) non-ASCII ratio and Latin/Cyrillic-Greek mixed-word count, (c) unique-word ratio, (d) spaced-punctuation density (' , ' + ' . ') per word. Drop the doc if any of these holds: more than 15% of its segments (or at least 2 segments for docs with under 14 segments) have hit rate below the existing valley threshold; any segment has non-ASCII ratio above thr_na or at least 3 mixed-script words; any segment has unique-word ratio under 0.2; any segment has punctuation density under 0.5*thr_dens (non-wiki text spliced in); a spam phrase appears anywhere in the full text (already full-text, keep). Also replace the doc-level rate1 in the score with the minimum segment hit rate, so that if the kept set exceeds T the cleanest docs are chosen. Leave everything else (classifier, gate, dedup, no-padding fill, seeded shuffle) unchanged. Add a time guard: if elapsed time exceeds 120 s, skip the remaining docs and keep their existing head-only verdict.
history.outcome: dev 1.8308 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace cycling with a 'general English first, target last' fill when the kept set is under T. Keep the current pipeline unchanged up to the `kept` list (clean, deduped, gated wiki-style docs). Then, only if est tokens of kept < 0.97*T: build a filler set from the remaining docs that are `~bad & ~shuf & ~keep`, not duplicates (reuse is_dup), have at least 100 words, a duplicate-line fraction under 0.3 (split on '\n', count lines of 20+ chars that repeat within the doc; this drops 'Home | About | Products' nav boilerplate), a unique-word ratio of at least 0.35 over the first 300 words, and at least 0.75 alphabetic-or-space chars in the first 3000. Also exclude wiki-style docs flagged as shuffled (already covered by ~shuf) and any doc containing 'click here to order', 'best price', 'online store' or 'limited offer'. Rank the filler by classifier `dec` descending and take just enough to bring the estimated total to 0.98*T (never more). Output order: filler docs first (seeded shuffle among themselves), then all kept wiki docs (seeded shuffle among themselves), so no target-domain doc is cut by the T limit and the final, low-learning-rate part of training is pure target-domain text. If kept >= 0.97*T, behave exactly as now. Drop the old 0.35*T top-up branch since this subsumes it.
history.outcome: dev 2.1361 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Add a target-calibrated anomaly filter on the already-kept docs, to catch damage types the current checks miss (character-level noise/typos, case damage, stripped or doubled whitespace, digit/markup-heavy list pages); leave everything else unchanged. Apply it after `keep` is computed and before dedup. For each target_sample doc and each kept pool doc, compute over the full text (cap 20,000 chars, taken as first 10k + last 10k so tail damage is seen): (a) chars per GPT-2 token using tiktoken encode_batch (corrupted words split into many tokens, so this ratio falls); (b) OOV rate = fraction of lowercase alphabetic word tokens that are not in a vocabulary V, where V = words appearing in the target sample or in at least 3 distinct kept pool docs (for target docs use the same V); (c) fraction of letters that are uppercase; (d) fraction of chars that are digits; (e) mean word length; (f) fraction of whitespace-separated tokens that are single characters other than punctuation. For each statistic take the target sample's median and MAD plus its 1st and 99th percentiles; define the allowed range as [min(p1, med - 6*MAD), max(p99, med + 6*MAD)], widened by 10% of (p99 - p1) on each side. Drop a kept doc if any statistic falls outside its range. Safety: if this would remove more than 25% of kept tokens, disable the filter entirely (thresholds are presumably miscalibrated). Skip docs under 100 words for (b). Also use the exact tiktoken counts where available instead of the chars/ratio estimate. Time guard: skip the filter if elapsed time is over 130 s.
history.outcome: dev 1.8267 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Fix a likely recall loss in the classifier gate, with no change to the damage filters. Today the negatives are a random pool sample, which includes many clean wiki-style articles, so the classifier is partly trained to separate the 200 target docs from in-domain pool docs, and `dec >= gate` can then drop genuine clean articles. Change: (1) Compute the structural features before the classifier and build negatives only from pool docs that are clearly not wiki-style: `~title & (dens < thr_dens)`, or spam. Sample 3000 of them with the seeded rng and keep the two-half cross-fit. (2) Self-training round: after the shuffle detection, take up to 1500 pool docs with `title & wiki & ~shuf` (seeded sample), add their first 1500 chars as extra positives, and refit against the same non-wiki negatives. Cross-fit these too: split the added positives into two halves and score each half with the model that did not train on it. Use this `dec` for scoring, and recompute the gate from the held-out target chunks as now. (3) Gate bypass: `keep = wiki & ~shuf & ((dec >= gate) | (title & (rate1 >= thr1)))`, so a doc that starts with a '= Title =' line, has target-like spaced punctuation and passes the bigram shuffle check is never dropped by the classifier alone. If shuffle detection is off, the bypass is `title & hyph`. (4) Leave bad/spam/non-ASCII checks, dedup, the no-padding fill and the final seeded shuffle unchanged. Log (to stderr) the kept doc count and estimated kept tokens / T before and after, so the size of the effect is visible.
history.outcome: dev 1.8309 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Add a token-level cross-entropy trim on the kept set, applied after `keep` is computed and before dedup; leave everything else unchanged.

1. Tokenize with tiktoken gpt2 `encode_batch` (`disallowed_special=()`): all target_sample docs in full, and every kept pool doc capped at 24,000 chars taken as first 8k + middle 8k + last 8k.
2. Build a smoothed unigram token distribution: counts from target_sample tokens plus the counts from all kept pool docs down-weighted so the pool mass equals the target mass, with add-0.5 smoothing over the 50,257-token vocabulary.
3. For each doc compute bits per byte: bpb_doc = sum(-log2 p(tok)) / number of UTF-8 bytes of the tokenized text. Also compute it per 8k-char piece and take max_piece.
4. Calibrate on the target sample, scoring each target doc leave-one-out (subtract its own counts before scoring). Let m = median and s = 1.4826 * MAD of the target bpb_doc. Set thr = max(target 97th percentile, m + 3*s). Set thr_piece the same way from the target per-piece values, using the 99th percentile and m + 4*s.
5. Drop a kept doc if bpb_doc > thr or max_piece > thr_piece. These are docs dominated by rare or fragmented tokens: character noise, case or whitespace damage, number/list/table-heavy pages, foreign-language stretches.
6. Safety: if this removes more than 20% of kept tokens, raise both thresholds to the value that removes exactly 20% by bpb_doc rank. Skip the trim entirely if elapsed time exceeds 130 s.
7. Use the exact token counts from step 1 (scaled by full length / tokenized length) in place of the chars/ratio estimate.
8. Log to stderr: kept doc count and kept tokens / T before and after, and both thresholds.

The final order stays a seeded shuffle; no padding.
history.outcome: dev 1.8282 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, rejected
dev 1.8172 against 1.8300 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea:
Tighten precision on article identity, leaving the classifier, shuffle detection, trim and fill unchanged.

(1) Title requirement. Compute the fraction of target_sample docs matching the existing `_TITLE` regex at the start. If it is at least 0.95, require `title[i]` for a pool doc to be kept (`keep &= title`). This drops wiki-punctuated text that is not a whole article in the target format.

(2) Title-keyed dedup. Extract the first-line title, lowercased and whitespace-normalised. Group kept docs by title. Within a group, sort by `score - zN` descending and keep the best doc. Drop every other doc in the group unless it is genuinely different content: the Jaccard overlap of its set of distinct lowercase words (first 3000 words) with every already-kept member of the group is below 0.5. This removes near-duplicate, truncated or lightly damaged copies of an article whose first 200 chars differ, which the current head-hash dedup misses. Word-set Jaccard is insensitive to word order, so a shuffled copy that slipped past the detector is also matched to its clean twin.

(3) Content dedup across titles. For each kept doc, hash the normalised text of chars 1000-1400 and of the last 400 chars. Drop a doc whose mid-hash or tail-hash was already seen in a higher-ranked doc (only for docs of at least 2000 chars).

Run (1) before the trim, and (2)-(3) in place of / in addition to the existing `is_dup` pass, which stays. Log to stderr: the target title fraction, docs dropped by each of the three rules, and K/T after.
history.outcome: dev 1.8206 against 1.8172 for the best at the time, rejected
dev 1.8423 against 1.8172 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Turn the hard trim into a two-tier scheme so that borderline in-domain docs are seen once instead of never, while clean docs keep their repeat passes. Leave the classifier, shuffle detection, spam/non-ASCII checks, dedup and the K >= T branch unchanged.

(1) Candidate set. Run `_trim_stats` on `cand = wiki & ~shuf & ((dec >= gate) | (title & hyph & (rate1 >= thr1)))` instead of on `keep`. If shuffle detection is off, the bypass is `title & hyph`. This gives gate-failed but clearly article-formatted docs their statistics and exact token counts.

(2) Three tiers from the trim result (`outs`, `z`):
- CLEAN: `dec >= gate` and no statistic outside its range. This matches today's kept set, except when the 15% cap binds.
- ONCE: (a) docs with `dec >= gate` and exactly one statistic outside its range with z <= 3.0, plus (b) gate-bypass docs with no statistic outside its range.
- DROP: everything else (two or more statistics out, z > 3, or a bypass doc with any exceedance).
Remove the 15% MAX_DROP cap logic. As a safety net, if CLEAN holds under 50% of candidate tokens, fall back to the current behaviour.

(3) Dedup. Apply the existing `is_dup` over CLEAN first in score order, then over ONCE, so a ONCE doc never displaces a CLEAN twin.

(4) Fill when K = tokens(CLEAN) < T:
- Let W = tokens(ONCE), capped at 0.20*T. If over the cap, keep the highest `score - z`.
- n_full = max(1, floor((T - W) / K)); rem = T - W - n_full*K.
- Output first a single seeded-shuffled block containing all ONCE docs plus, if rem > 0, the partial pass of the highest-score CLEAN docs covering rem + 0.005*T.
- Then output n_full full passes over CLEAN, each with its own seeded shuffle as now.
ONCE docs therefore appear exactly once and only in the early part of training; the final passes are purely CLEAN.

(5) Log to stderr: doc count and tokens/T for CLEAN, ONCE(a), ONCE(b) and DROP, then W/T, n_full and rem/T.
history.outcome: dev 1.8151 against 1.8172 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Add a see-once early block of extra in-domain text ahead of the clean repeat passes, extending the two-tier idea of experiment 10 (which measured 1.8151) with a new source: word-shuffled wiki articles. Classifier, shuffle detection, spam/non-ASCII checks, dedup and the K >= T branch stay unchanged.

(1) Candidates. Run `_trim_stats` on `cand = wiki & ((dec >= gate) | (title & hyph))`, which now includes docs flagged `shuf`. Every candidate gets its six statistics and an exact token count.

(2) Tiers.
- CLEAN: `~shuf & dec >= gate` and no statistic outside its 5s range. Remove the 15% MAX_DROP cap. If CLEAN holds under 50% of the non-shuffled candidate tokens, fall back to the current behaviour.
- ONCE_A: `~shuf & dec >= gate` with exactly one statistic out and z <= 3.0, plus `~shuf` gate-bypass docs (`title & hyph & rate1 >= thr1`) with no statistic out.
- ONCE_S: `shuf & title & (dec >= gate)` docs with no statistic outside its range. These are in-domain articles whose only damage is word order; tokens, vocabulary, spelling and formatting are intact.
- DROP: everything else.

(3) Dedup with the existing `is_dup`, in the order CLEAN (by score), then ONCE_A, then ONCE_S. For ONCE_S, also drop a doc whose normalised first-line title equals the title of any CLEAN or ONCE_A doc, so a shuffled copy never duplicates an article already present clean.

(4) Fill when K = tokens(CLEAN) < T.
- Cap ONCE_S at 0.12*T and ONCE_A at 0.15*T, keeping the highest `score - z` in each. Let W = the sum of both.
- n_full = max(1, floor((T - W) / K)); rem = T - W - n_full*K.
- Output order:
  a. all ONCE_S docs, seeded shuffle, at the very start (warm-up steps);
  b. one seeded-shuffled block of ONCE_A plus, if rem > 0, the partial pass of the highest-score CLEAN docs covering rem + 0.005*T;
  c. n_full full CLEAN passes, each with its own seeded shuffle.
- If ONCE_S is empty or shuffle detection is off, this reduces to experiment 10.

(5) Log to stderr: docs and tokens/T for CLEAN, ONCE_A, ONCE_S and DROP, then W/T, n_full and rem/T.
history.outcome: dev 1.8801 against 1.8172 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Re-run the two-tier scheme of experiment 10 (the lowest measured value, 1.8151) with a wider see-once tier and the see-once docs spread through the first pass instead of packed at the start. Classifier, shuffle detection, spam/non-ASCII checks, `is_dup` and the K >= T branch stay unchanged.

(1) Candidates. Run `_trim_stats` on `cand = wiki & ~shuf & ((dec >= gate) | (title & hyph & (rate1 >= thr1)))`. If shuffle detection is off, the bypass is `title & hyph`. Shuffled docs are never candidates.

(2) Tiers from `outs` and `z`:
- CLEAN: `dec >= gate` and no statistic outside its 5s range. Remove the 15% MAX_DROP cap.
- ONCE: (a) `dec >= gate` docs with one or two statistics out and z <= 4.0; (b) gate-bypass docs with at most one statistic out and z <= 2.0.
- DROP: everything else.
- Safety: if CLEAN holds under 50% of candidate tokens, fall back to the current behaviour (capped trim, no ONCE tier).

(3) Dedup. Apply `is_dup` over CLEAN in score order first, then over ONCE in `score - z` order, so a ONCE doc never displaces a CLEAN twin.

(4) Fill when K = tokens(CLEAN) < T:
- Cap ONCE at W <= 0.20*T, keeping the highest `score - z`.
- n_full = max(1, floor((T - W) / K)); rem = T - W - n_full*K.
- If n_full >= 2: output first the partial pass of the highest-score CLEAN docs covering rem + 0.005*T (seeded shuffle, only if rem > 0). Then output one seeded-shuffled block that is the union of all ONCE docs and one full CLEAN pass, so ONCE text is interleaved with clean text. Then output the remaining n_full - 1 pure CLEAN passes, each with its own seeded shuffle.
- If n_full == 1: output one seeded-shuffled block of the partial CLEAN docs plus ONCE, then one full CLEAN pass.
- In both cases ONCE docs appear exactly once and the last pass is purely CLEAN.

(5) Use exact token counts for all candidates. Log to stderr: docs and tokens/T for CLEAN, ONCE(a), ONCE(b) and DROP, then W/T, n_full and rem/T.
history.outcome: dev 1.8148 against 1.8172 for the best at the time, rejected
